title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 7-9). Grothendieck works with a 'de Rham complex with divided powers' C^{..}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) of a simplicial (or semi-simplicial) object X_* over an arbitrary base ring k. It is defined as Hom(O_{X_*}, C^{..}_{DRpd,*}(k)), where C^{..}_{DRpd,*}(k) is a simplicial bigraded differential k{T}-algebra built from divided-power polynomial forms on the standard simplices. Here k{T} = S is the divided-power algebra in one variable T, used in a homogeneous or 'parametrised' version (C(X_*; k{T}, k{T}^+, T)).

The bidegrees are:
- p, a divided-power weight: C^{p,q} = Gamma^p(L) ⊗ Lambda^q(Psi), with L the simplicial module of linear coordinates and Psi the differentials.
- q, the exterior (form) degree.

On page 7 he shows, in each total degree n:
- C^{p,q}_* is contractible ('cyclique') for p ≠ 0.
- The rows give a length-n resolution of the constant k_* by acyclic half-simplicial k-modules, except the last term. So it is a truncation of a flasque resolution.
- Taking sections over X_* gives H^{p,q}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) ≅ H^q(X_*,k) for p ≥ 0, and 0 for p < 0.

This page asks for the k{T}-module structure for fixed q, i.e. how multiplication by T moves p to p+1. The answer is that H^{.,q} is the free divided-power module on H^q.
- First formula: H^{.,q}_{DRpd} ≅ tau_q(H^?(X_*,k) ⊗_k k{T})[q]. The index is written as H^0, but H^q is meant. The truncation keeps total degrees ≥ q; the shift [q] translates degrees by -q.
- Reindexing by (total degree n, exterior degree q) with p = n - q: H'^{n,q} = H^{n-q,q}. The degree condition p, q ≥ 0 becomes n ≥ q ≥ 0, and the differential has bidegree (0,1).
- Result: H'^{.,q}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) ≅ tau_q(H^q(X_*,k) ⊗_k k{T}). Here H^q ⊗ T^{[p]} sits in total degree q+p.
- These isomorphisms are multiplicative (cup product tensored with the divided-power multiplication of k{T}) and functorial in X_* and k.

The closing remark says that a priori the bigraded object does not hand you the k-modules H^q and their cup pairings directly. It hands you the graded S-modules tau_q(H^q ⊗ S) and the pairings among them induced by the cup product.

This sets up page 9's 'théorie des ombres' (theory of shadows): a graded k-module M, and a pairing M⊗N→P, can be recovered canonically from the truncations tau_q(M⊗S) and the induced pairings, for q large relative to the degrees of M. So the bigraded differential S-algebra C^{..}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) determines the graded cohomology algebra H^*(X_*,k). He then hopes it determines more:
- RGamma(X_*,k) as an object of D(k) with its multiplicative structure;
- ultimately the full homotopy type of X_*, over any k, as Sullivan's polynomial forms do over Q.

The problem served is an integral or arbitrary-coefficient analogue of Sullivan's rational homotopy theory, using divided powers to make the Poincaré lemma work in positive and mixed characteristic.
errors: The first displayed formula writes H^0(X_*,k) ⊗ k{T}, where from page 7 and the later formula it should be H^q(X_*,k) (fixed q). This is probably a slip, or an ambiguous glyph in the image.

Two notations for the same object are mixed. The version with [q] (shift) and the reindexed H' version describe it differently; tau_q 'truncated in degree ≥ q' is automatic once H^q is placed in degree q. The notation is loose but not wrong.

As written, the remark 'on a récupérer' is incoherent; the sense must be 'on ne récupère pas a priori … mais …'. It is substantively trivial anyway: the bidegree (n,q) = (q,q) component of H' is literally H^q. So 'recovering' H^* from the bigraded algebra is easy. The non-trivial hope (page 9) is recovering homotopy information, not cohomology.

Over a general k, multiplication by T sends T^{[p]} to (p+1)T^{[p+1]}, so it is not injective in positive characteristic. The phrase 'k{T}-module structure' hides this torsion, though the formula H^q ⊗ k{T} handles it correctly.

ideas.what: Simplicial divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on standard simplices over an arbitrary ring k, giving a cochain functor on simplicial sets or schemes
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power (PD) analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial forms A_PL; integral de Rham theorem with divided powers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) over Q. Integral variants: Cenkl–Porter (early 1980s, forms with controlled denominators); divided-power de Rham complexes in crystalline theory (Berthelot, Illusie). Homotopy-type recovery: Mandell (E_infinity cochains, 2001/2006), Toën (affine stacks/schematization, 2006, 2020), Horel and Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov (binomial rings, 2020s)
ideas.where_published: The schematization problem appears in Pursuing Stacks (1983). The 1976 IHÉS talk on the PD de Rham complex is not, to my knowledge, published.

ideas.what: Bigraded computation H^{p,q}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) ≅ H^q(X_*,k) for p ≥ 0, with k{T}-module structure H'^{.,q} ≅ H^q ⊗_k k{T} (free divided-power module), compatible with cup products
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology of a graded/homogenised (Rees-type) PD de Rham model; H^* ⊗ Gamma(T) as a module over the divided-power algebra

ideas.what: Reindexing by (total degree, exterior degree) so that the differential has bidegree (0,1) and the degree condition becomes n ≥ q ≥ 0
ideas.modern_name: Regrading of a bicomplex / weight-degree bookkeeping

ideas.what: Recovering a graded module or algebra and its pairings from the truncations tau_q(M ⊗ S) over the divided-power algebra S ('théorie des ombres', set up here, stated on next page)
ideas.modern_name: No standard name; loosely related to Rees/filtration–degeneration arguments and to recovering objects from PD-envelopes

missed.claim: Around 1975-76 Grothendieck pursued an arbitrary-coefficient (integral, mod p) analogue of Sullivan's rational de Rham models via divided-power polynomial forms. The aim was full homotopy information through a bigraded differential S-algebra (S = k{T}). This predates Cenkl–Porter's integral de Rham models, Mandell's E_infinity cochain theorems and Toën's affine stacks. The setup here is a homogenised PD model graded by divided-power weight, with an extra divided-power parameter T. It is a specific mechanism not used in that later literature, which proceeds via E_infinity, cosimplicial or binomial structures.
missed.quote: H'^{.,q}_{DRpd}(X_x,k) ≃ tau_q(H^q(X_x,k) ⊗_k k{T}) … Ces isomorphismes sont compatibles avec les structures multiplicatives
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work on integral homotopy via binomial or divided-power structures (Horel; Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov; Toën's revisit of schematization) could compare with this weight-graded PD model. The question is whether the weight grading plus the T-module structure carries the extra power-operation data that plain PD forms lose.

missed.claim: The 'theory of shadows' is announced (next page) as an assumed tool: graded algebras are recovered from the truncated S-algebras tau_q(H ⊗ S). The program to recover RGamma(X_*,k) with its multiplicative structure, and then the homotopy type, is left as a hope.
missed.quote: Donc a priori … les k-modules gradués tau_q(H^q(X_x,k)⊗_k k{T}) et leurs accouplements déduits du cup
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether a PD-weight-graded cochain model detects Steenrod operations or the p-adic homotopy type is a concrete open-style question. Known obstructions are that strictly commutative models fail in characteristic p, so Steenrod operations must appear via the divided powers or the weight grading.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation on this page is routine: the bigraded cohomology is the free divided-power module on H^q, compatible with cup products. What is notable is the documented 1976 program of a divided-power Sullivan-type model over arbitrary rings, with an explicit hope of recovering homotopy type. This predates the published integral-homotopy literature and is only partially reflected in Grothendieck's later Pursuing Stacks schematization remarks. That context is of historical interest, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the subscript object is the simplicial X_* (written X_x in the transcription); likewise throughout.
First displayed formula: the image shows H°(X_*,k) ⊗_k k{T}. The intended object is presumably H^q(X_*,k), consistent with the later formula.

'(égal au degré cartésien . plus q)' and 'couple (degré total, degré cartésien)': the handwritten word is unclear and 'cartésien' is doubtful. It refers to the divided-power weight degree p, possibly 'degré cosimplicial' or similar; the next page calls q the 'extérieur' degree.
'(dans la condition de degré p,q≥0 devient n≥q≥0' should read '(donc la condition de degré p,q ≥ 0 devient n ≥ q ≥ 0'.
'dans l'ensemble (ensemble gradué) de S-modules gradués' is likely 'dans l'… (bigradué) de S-modules gradués'; the words are uncertain.

'Donc a priori (on a … récupérer par les k-modules' should read 'Donc a priori on ne récupère pas (via H'…) les k-modules H^q(X_*,k) et leurs cup-accouplements, mais les k-modules gradués tau_q(…) et leurs accouplements déduits du cup'.
